cast.mascot: small hero, red cape, round head

beats.say: In Japan, bullet trains start braking before the earthquake shaking even arrives.
The trick: every earthquake sends out two kinds of waves.
The P-wave comes first. It is fast, but weak.
The S-wave follows. It is slower, and it is the one that shakes the ground hard.
Seismometers along the coast and the tracks listen for that first P-wave.
The moment they feel it, the system cuts power to the overhead lines.
With no power, every train brakes automatically, seconds before the S-wave hits.
In 2011, during Japan's biggest recorded earthquake, the bullet trains in the region stopped, and no passenger on them was hurt.
